approach.method_basis: The Parent draws atom, bond, path and ring edits from one scored current molecule, normalizes the resulting isomeric identity, rejects duplicates and directly evaluates a full batch admitted by inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when its score worsens, with a separate best archive. The current atom-change operator chooses an eligible atom and then an alternative element; it can erase configuration during substitution but never offers a configuration-only edit. Local memory descriptions omit stereochemistry, while full molecular identity already retains it. The repaired identity join and existing memory lifecycle remain part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Add local assignment or inversion of one eligible tetrahedral carbon as an option within the existing atom-change menu. An unassigned center offers both orientations; an assigned center offers its opposite orientation. Every such option preserves atomic composition and connectivity. Element substitutions remain available and the atom-change allocation weight stays fixed. This tests whether explicitly different configurations can reach evaluation and influence the observed walk. Earlier siblings changed sulfur eligibility and pendant-branch deletion; neither introduced a stereochemical edit, and neither is incorporated into this Child.

observed_bottleneck: The complete Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 has macro mean 0.5209178281192797 and standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. Its fifteen saved task logs and molecular assessments contain no explicit carbon stereochemistry in any of 4350 emitted neighbors, despite frequent substituted saturated rings and side chains. The source changes atom identity and can clear a chiral tag, but never assigns or inverts one. An offline audit with the registered RDKit potential-center rule finds eligible tetrahedral-carbon centers in 273 of 435 batch-start graphs, totaling 547 center occurrences and 1094 two-way assignment options across these repeated states. All 1094 normalized products are graph-valid, differ isomerically from their source, retain its nonstereochemical graph and are fresh at that batch boundary. Among 1455 actual change_atom draws, 941 occur in a graph with a stereo option, but only 55 select an eligible center; availability therefore does not guarantee use. No new scores were obtained. The sulfur sibling n-93cd9a000278 retains unspecified stereochemistry after its chemistry gate, and n-0e56e71777c4 reaches compact neighbors but loses score in every replica without resolving stereochemistry. These siblings do not test configuration-only neighbors. The hypothesized limitation is an absent local stereochemical proposal channel, not established oracle sensitivity to stereoisomers.
hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing atom-change menu with single-center tetrahedral-carbon configuration assignment or inversion, preserving the molecular composition and connectivity while allowing canonically distinct stereochemical neighbors to enter the unchanged novelty, tabu and accepted-score walk.

finding_summary.headline: Carbon configuration assignments reach evaluation, but every direct score comparison ties
finding_summary.insights: The missing configuration channel was a real generator limitation: it can now supply fresh evaluated identities without breaking the repaired identity join or changing graph chemistry. Its immediate effect here was neutral movement through differently annotated states. Because the inherited local motifs omit stereochemistry, all nine selected assignment moves advanced memory age without installing new inverse restrictions. Such moves can alter later search even when their own scores tie; later endpoint differences therefore do not demonstrate a preference for either configuration. The equal scores establish a limitation for the sampled unspecified-to-assigned comparisons only. No opposite fully assigned pair was evaluated, so the response to genuine configuration inversion remains open. The molecular assessment also shows that stereochemical labels leave the pre-existing aromatic, reactive-heteroatom and densely bridged sulfur-rich chemistry largely intact. Partial assignments neither resolve all centers nor establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility. The experiment narrows the next scientific question to whether configuration coverage can have useful measured consequences under this feedback and walk, rather than whether the generator can emit it.
finding_summary.results: All 24 configuration-only edits reached evaluation as distinct molecular identities while preserving composition and connectivity. Each assigned one previously unspecified carbon center; both relative orientations were sampled, but no assigned-center inversion was selected. Nine of these neighbors became the next current molecule with exactly the same score as their source. Assignments also survived many subsequent structural edits: 488 of 4,350 emitted neighbors contained an assigned carbon center, compared with none for the parent. Across 32 actually evaluated pairs sharing the same graph but differing in the extent of stereochemical assignment, every pair received equal scalar feedback. The complete three-seed mean nevertheless fell from 0.520918 to 0.511159, a paired change of -0.009759, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.013487, +0.001052 and -0.043817; the main losses were in DRD2 and sitagliptin, while median improved slightly and the other two task means were unchanged. The proposal mechanism activated, but this panel does not support its score usefulness.

molecular.headline: Partial stereochemical labels decorate aromatic amines, reactive heteroatoms and densely bridged sulfur-rich structures
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories cover every objective and every supplied seed, with 900 molecules read and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Ring-closure tokens occur in every proposal; aromatic-token rates range from 0.7299 to 1.0. These are ring-rich, generally medium-sized to bulky molecules, including conventional fused heteroaromatic amides, halogenated aryl amines, flexible heterocyclic diones and elaborate bridged sulfur-containing cages. Mean SMILES lengths range from 48.0 to 72.0, and the proposals remain substantial ring-bearing structures. Compared with the supplied parent, the present strings include stereochemical labels: task rates are 0.1379, 0.0023, 0.1023, 0.223 and 0.0954 in the fixed task order, while the parent trajectory strings contain no @ symbols. This is partial stereochemical specification; many leading molecules and other possible stereogenic centres remain unassigned. All charged-token rates are 0.0, which does not establish that the depicted amines would be neutral in solution. The overall chemical diversity is moderate across families and seeds, with strong local concentration within related ring frameworks. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable because unusual substituted, multiply bonded sulfur, N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxide variants and dense ring junctions persist beside more ordinary medicinal chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring molecules are relatively compact fused aromatic or partly saturated heterocycles bearing an aryl amide or ketone. The leading benzofuran-like structure has methyl groups, a thiol, an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro aryl amide. A close-scoring indole carboxanilide instead combines an ordinary amide with ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents. Other leading families contain benzothiophene-like rings, pyridyl ketones, N-fluoro groups or stereolabelled O/N-bridged frameworks. The low examples often disrupt an aromatic ring or replace the carbonyl-containing connection with a less organized, partly saturated arrangement. The indole amide is a plausible synthetic family; N-halogenated cage relatives require substantially more caution.
liabilities: N-chloro amides and amines, N-fluoro groups and amino-chloromethyl substituents introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl halogenation.
Free thiols and unusual substituted sulfur occur alongside dense ring junctions; chemical stability and practical access cannot be inferred from their SMILES.
missing_features: Low-scoring ring-expanded or carbonyl-replaced derivatives lack the intact aromatic carbonyl arrangement present in the higher-scoring indole and benzofuran families.

The leading set provides limited coverage of straightforward aromatic amide relatives without reactive nitrogen substituents; the near-leading ordinary indole amide shows that such chemistry is already compatible with a high observed score.
Many bridged centres remain unspecified even when one stereochemical label is present. The displayed equal-score pair supplies no evidence for a particular preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzofuran-like N-chloro amide scores 0.41003927643747895, while the less elaborated indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. The initial substituted indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. A derivative that replaces its carbonyl connection by an aminoalkyl arrangement scores 0.03343008011310944, and an expanded sulfur-containing ring example scores 0.023463222457063. This associates higher scores with retaining a compact aromatic carbonyl framework, without showing that the reactive N-halogen groups are necessary. The unlabelled and stereolabelled bridged pair at evaluations 165 and 173 both score 0.3923638265355735. The best molecules and best scores in each seed match the corresponding parent seed; the late stereolabelled cages therefore add visible chemical specification without establishing a preferred configuration from these paired scores.

per_task.generated_character: These are bulky aromatic heterocycles with extensive peripheral decoration. The leading family combines a substituted phenyl group, an amino-fluoroalkyl connection, a fused nitrogen heterocycle containing carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, imines and a long ether/thioether-rich chain. Some members carry an N-bromo substituent or an S-chloro terminus, and a multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centre links another side chain. The final seed-2 family instead has a heteroaromatic dione, an unsaturated carbon chain and a fused aza/ether ring with acetal-like substitution. Early low-scoring structures are less decorated ester/phenol-containing relatives or disrupted fused-ring systems. Size, flexible heteroatom-rich appendages and the unusual sulfur connections make the leading family less straightforward to synthesize than its recognizable individual fragments suggest.
liabilities: Long mixed ether/thioether chains add flexibility and chemical complexity without a demonstrated local score advantage for several extensions.
N-bromo and S-chloro variants add reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds; multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur is not an ordinary thioether or sulfone.
Cumulated unsaturation appears in a low-scoring ring variant, while high-scoring unsaturated side chains lack alkene geometry specification.
missing_features: The lower-scoring distorted ring systems lack the retained aromatic heterocyclic organization of the higher-scoring decorated families.

Less elaborate relatives that preserve the useful core and substitute ordinary stable connections for the unusual sulfur linkage are not represented among the displayed leaders. Equal scores for several peripheral variants leave room for chemical simplification, but do not prove its score outcome.
Configuration is almost wholly unspecified despite branched side chains and acetal-like centres; the stereocentre-token rate is only 0.0023.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated structure scores 0.6161710037174721 versus 0.548381482770623 for the initial aromatic dione. Early ring-disrupted or carbonyl-altered derivatives score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063. Several later variants retain exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite changing an alkyl substituent, extending a sulfur-bound alkyl group, replacing N-methyl with N-bromo, or adding side-chain branching. Thus the visible improvement accompanies retention of the decorated aromatic core, while these peripheral changes have little demonstrated chemical specificity. The final aza/ether-ring family reaches 0.6092182584436399, including both oxygen- and sulfur-containing side-chain variants. The corresponding parent has the same leading structures and per-seed best scores.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring seed-0 family contains halogenated aromatic groups around a fused saturated nitrogen ring system with tertiary amines and an exocyclic amino substituent. Methoxy, fluoromethyl and bromo substituents provide a substantial hydrophobic surface. A terminal methylene is double-bonded to sulfur that also bears carbon substituents, so this is not an ordinary thiocarbonyl linker. The low examples are bulky biaryl carboxylic acids containing amide and sulfonamide functionality, with much less freely basic nitrogen. Other seeds produce more sulfur-rich polycycles; the final seed-2 molecules combine amines, halogenated aryl groups, sulfur/nitrogen rings and partial stereochemical labels. Ordinary aryl-amine fragments are recognizable, but unusual sulfur bonding and complex ring junctions weaken the plausibility of the assembled molecules.
liabilities: Unusual sulfur valence and occasional extended nitrogen chains accompany otherwise familiar aryl amine fragments.
Multiple potentially basic centres and substantial halogenated aromatic surface are combined without any observed ionization or solubility characterization.
Partial stereochemical labels leave other ring-junction relationships unresolved, especially in the more elaborate sulfur-rich families.
missing_features: The low-scoring acid/amide/sulfonamide structures lack the accessible aliphatic amine pattern present in the highest-scoring molecules.

The displayed high-scoring amine frameworks lack a matched series with conventional stable linkers replacing multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur; the observed amine association does not establish a need for that sulfur representation.
The leading fused-ring molecule does not specify its stereochemistry, and a labelled/unlabelled comparison elsewhere in the same family has equal scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-substituted fused-ring molecule scores 0.9947772153531709. Its methyl-bearing relative scores 0.9889929682046574, and replacing the exocyclic amino substituent with carbon gives 0.9829362789697462. The corresponding stereolabelled carbon-substituted molecule also scores 0.9829362789697462. These observations associate high scores with an aryl-rich aliphatic amine framework and show tolerance for local substitution, without identifying a stereochemical preference. The carboxylic acid/amide/sulfonamide examples score 0.007468397818197266 to 0.011875520467584314. Compared with the parent, seed 0 now has a different amine-ring family and a best score of 0.9947772153531709 versus 0.8856242185485628; seed 2 has a different sulfur-rich family and reaches 0.7028857845781294 versus 0.9148143511682032. Those mixed molecular outcomes do not isolate which individual structural change explains the score.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are medium-to-bulky polycycles combining an alkyl-substituted aza-aromatic ring, another aryl group, unsaturation, a cyclic carbonyl and N/O-rich ring closures. The best example bears a phenol and several methylated nitrogen centres; close relatives contain an N-O bridge, an N-N connection or an O-O connection. Lower early examples retain an ester/phenol-substituted aromatic group and a pyrrole-like ring but open the dicarbonyl-containing ring into a more flexible chain. Other low and final examples include O-bromo substituents, sulfur-bound bromine, partly labelled ring junctions and unusual sulfur-containing bridges. Several ordinary amide and aromatic fragments are present, but the assembled bridged structures are synthetically demanding and sometimes chemically reactive.
liabilities: N-O, N-N and O-O bridges can introduce labile or reactive connections within already complex polycycles.
O-bromo groups, sulfur-bound bromine and unusual substituted sulfur occur in alternative families without resolving the remaining structural fit.
Dense ring closures and incompletely specified junctions make practical synthesis and conformational feasibility uncertain.
missing_features: The lower ring-opened structures lack the constrained aryl/carbonyl arrangement retained in the leading polycycles.

The displayed high-scoring relatives do not establish a chemically necessary role for N-N or O-O connections. Simpler stable ring connections that retain the same spatial organization remain incompletely represented.
Some structures now specify a stereocentre, but full relative configuration across the bridged framework is missing and equal-score examples do not identify a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading phenol-containing polycycle scores 0.2107445781802027, versus 0.1678386594791329 for the initial aromatic dione and 0.12467972074136988 or 0.1263981386214515 for ring-opened carbonyl-chain relatives. An N-N-containing ring, a carbon-containing connection and another nitrogen-containing connection all appear at 0.20775769309691736; an O-O-containing relative remains close at 0.20647766243219587. This favors the overall aryl/carbonyl/polycyclic organization more clearly than it favors the unusual local heteroatom bonds. The labelled and unlabelled pair at 0.2056349053193895 is identical in score. Parent seed 0 and seed 2 retain the same best structures and scores; the changed seed-1 family reaches 0.19618123146095062 versus 0.19092251395438758, while still carrying reactive O-Br and sulfur-bound bromine.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact but exceptionally ring-dense sulfur-rich cages bearing fluorinated carbon sites and an embedded nitrogen-containing dione. A thioether-linked fluorohydrin-like substituent, an NH group, methyl groups and several multiply bonded sulfur centres recur. The higher-scoring structures retain both carbonyl and fluorinated carbon features while changing sulfur bridges and ring closures. Low-scoring early molecules include more extended aromatic diones as well as already elaborate sulfur-containing structures, so sulfur content or ring density alone does not distinguish success. Final seed-2 products have partly specified stereochemistry, carbonyl groups, N-fluoro imine-containing substituents and still more constrained sulfur frameworks. These are chemically questionable assemblies despite their moderate overall size.
liabilities: Multiply bonded sulfur with additional substituents, S-H-containing unsaturated rings and extensive bridging raise substantial stability and synthesis questions.
Direct N-F bonds and heteroatom-rich reactive substituents remain in alternative families.
Several ring fusions and unsaturated bridges are densely packed; stereochemical annotation alone does not demonstrate a geometrically accessible cage.
missing_features: Lower-scoring carbonyl-to-imino and carbon-bound-to-nitrogen-bound fluorine variants fail to retain the specific carbonyl/fluorinated-carbon arrangement of their higher-scoring relatives.

The reported leading family lacks convincing conventional-valence, less constrained ring systems that preserve those observed polar and fluorinated features; these trajectories do not establish whether such replacements would improve the score.
The best cage has no stereochemical labels. Labels on later molecules leave substantial ring-junction relationships unassigned and supply no matched evidence of a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated dione cage scores 0.5903526424693334. A close ring variant retains 0.5486087229725075. Replacing a carbonyl by an imino group in the displayed related pair reduces the score from 0.519850349488241 to 0.48440391849409126; replacing N-fluoromethyl by direct N-fluorination in another pair gives 0.47934323658895966 versus 0.5091666078884868. These comparisons support retention and placement of carbonyl and carbon-bound fluorine within the observed family, rather than a benefit from indiscriminately adding heteroatom-bound fluorine. Early expanded dione and sulfur-rich structures score as low as 7.590554525032884e-10 and 1.0546805269255595e-09. The parent retains the same leading seed-1 molecule and score. Current seed-0 and seed-2 maxima are 0.43947060890356343 and 0.4413006791220245, compared with parental 0.48118636011729826 and 0.4484554129767839; the chemistry remains dominated by elaborate sulfur cages.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre-token rates span 0.0023 to 0.223, and the displayed leaders often remain unlabelled. Several exact labelled/unlabelled pairs share scores, including 0.3923638265355735, 0.9829362789697462 and 0.2056349053193895. The parent strings contain no @ symbols, so the present labels are real additional output detail, but they neither define all potentially stereogenic sites nor establish a preferred configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical specification is partial and is not yet tied to fully defined, feasible ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically consistent relative and absolute configurations for feasible stereogenic frameworks, preserve those assignments through structural changes, and compare matched configurations through the existing score interface without presuming that the presence of a label itself has value.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aryl amine leaders use a terminal methylene double-bonded to additionally carbon-substituted sulfur; other leading and low families include N-Cl, N-F, N-Br, O-Br, sulfur-bound halogens, peroxide connections and densely bridged sulfur. An ordinary indole amide already scores 0.39905049777278273, demonstrating that a relatively simple conventional bonding pattern can also be competitive within the observed set.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring fragment arrangements remain coupled to unusual sulfur valence and reactive heteroatom bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched conventional-valence linkers and stable heteroatom substitutions that retain useful aryl, amine and carbonyl arrangements. Chemical alternatives should be available alongside structural exploration, with their relevance determined by observed feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring examples repeatedly disrupt aromatic carbonyl frameworks or open a constrained carbonyl ring, whereas related higher-scoring molecules retain those arrangements. At the other extreme, many proposals add densely fused or bridged heteroatom-rich rings whose three-dimensional feasibility is unresolved.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful local organization when changing ring size or core connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand access to ordinary ring sizes, stable fused systems and less constrained connections while preserving promising local functional-group arrangements. Changes should offer meaningful scaffold alternatives without relying on indiscriminate ring expansion or dense cage formation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several decorated heterocycles share 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension, branching or N-methyl-to-N-bromo substitution. Related polycycles with carbon or nitrogen connections share 0.20775769309691736, while a peroxide-containing variant remains close at 0.20647766243219587. These observations do not establish that the extra flexible chains or reactive bonds are needed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simpler alternatives are underrepresented where local score comparisons tolerate substantial peripheral or heteroatom changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched simplifications that reduce flexible appendages, reactive bonds or unnecessary heteroatom connections while preserving the principal molecular framework. Use score observations to decide which reductions retain useful chemistry.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
